caption:
Stoneware or earthenware: look at the foot before you buy.

Turn it over in the shop. The unglazed foot ring is the one place the clay itself shows. Dense, smooth, grey or buff usually means stoneware, fired hot enough to seal itself. Chalky, pale or orange usually means earthenware, sealed only by its glaze, so a chip at the rim drinks.

For a vase, either is fine. For what you eat from every day, stoneware.

Illustrated here so you know where to look. The foot on the shelf tells you the rest.

Save this for the ceramics aisle.
